meta.title: Our Services
meta.description: Lifecare brings two kinds of care home: Skilled Home Health for clinical recovery, and Provider Attendant Services for everyday support.

hero.headline: Two ways we bring care home.
hero.intro: Whether the need is clinical recovery or everyday support, Lifecare meets it at home, with the right professional for the job.

skilled.title: Skilled Home Health
skilled.description: Licensed clinicians bring hospital-grade skill into the home — nursing, therapy, and medical social work coordinated with your physician.

attendant.title: Provider Attendant Services
attendant.description: Trained attendants help with the everyday tasks that keep daily life safe, dignified, and independent at home.

skilled.title: Recovering from something?
skilled.body: If you're recovering from an illness, surgery, or a hospital stay, Skilled Home Health brings licensed clinicians to your door to manage that recovery.

attendant.title: Need a hand with daily life?
attendant.body: If the need is help with everyday tasks like bathing, meals, and errands, Provider Attendant Services brings a trained, consistent attendant into your home.

meta.title: Skilled Home Health
meta.description: Skilled nursing, physical, occupational, and speech therapy, medical social work, home health aide, and remote patient monitoring at home.

hero.headline: Skilled care, brought home.
hero.intro: Our nurses, therapists, and aides come to you, so you can recover where you are most comfortable, surrounded by family.

pillar.title: One skilled team, seven disciplines.
pillar.body: Your care plan may draw on any combination of these services. Our nurses coordinate with your physician so the right clinician is at your door on the right day.

detail.Stethoscope: Our RNs and LVNs assess wounds, manage medications, and support chronic disease management between your doctor visits.
detail.PersonSimpleWalk: Physical therapists help you regain strength, mobility, and balance after surgery, injury, or a progressive condition.
detail.HandHeart: Occupational therapists work on the everyday tasks that keep you safe and independent at home, like dressing, bathing, and cooking.
detail.ChatCircleDots: Speech therapists address communication and swallowing difficulties following stroke, neurological changes, or injury.
detail.UsersThree: Our social workers help families navigate benefits, find community resources, and coordinate the non-clinical side of a care plan.
detail.House: Certified home health aides assist with bathing, grooming, meal preparation, and the daily routines that matter most.
detail.Heartbeat: Connected home devices track your vital signs daily. Your nurse reviews the data and can respond quickly if something changes.

conditions.title: Clinical experience across a wide range of diagnoses.

start.title: When you call, here's what happens
start.intro: Reaching out shouldn't feel daunting. The first call is simple, human, and pressure-free.

step1.title: We listen
step1.body: A care coordinator answers, learns your situation, and helps you understand which skilled service fits.

step2.title: We coordinate
step2.body: We connect with your physician, arrange an in-home assessment, and handle the paperwork so your family doesn't have to.

step3.title: Care begins at home
step3.body: The right clinician starts a personalized plan of care, with ongoing oversight and a team you can reach whenever you need us.

cta.headline: Ready to bring care home?
cta.note: Call us and we'll walk you through coverage.

meta.title: Provider Attendant Services
meta.description: Trained attendants help with bathing, meals, light housekeeping, errands, and companionship, so your loved one can stay safe and comfortable at home.

hero.headline: A steady hand with everyday life, at home.
hero.intro: When the need is help with daily routines rather than clinical care, a trained attendant brings consistency, patience, and an extra set of hands into the home.

tasks.title: What an attendant helps with
tasks.body: Every attendant assignment is built around the person, not a checklist. Here is the kind of everyday help families ask for most.

bathing.title: Bathing, dressing & grooming
bathing.body: Help with the personal care routines that keep someone clean, comfortable, and dressed for the day.

meals.title: Meal preparation
meals.body: Planning and preparing meals that fit personal tastes and dietary needs.

housekeeping.title: Light housekeeping & laundry
housekeeping.body: Keeping the home tidy, dishes done, and laundry washed and put away.

errands.title: Errands & escort to appointments
errands.body: Grocery runs, pharmacy pickups, and a steady arm to and from appointments.

companionship.title: Companionship & a safe routine
companionship.body: Conversation, shared activities, and a familiar face that helps the day feel normal.

mobility.title: Mobility & transfer support
mobility.body: Help moving safely around the home, in and out of a chair or bed.

expect.title: What to expect
expect.intro: Bringing an attendant into your home is a big decision. Here is how we make it a comfortable one.

step1.title: A personalized care plan
step1.body: We start by learning the routines, preferences, and needs that matter to your family, and build the plan around them.

step2.title: A consistent attendant
step2.body: The same attendant returns visit after visit, so your loved one is cared for by someone who knows their routine.

step3.title: Regular oversight
step3.body: A supervisor checks in with regular visits to make sure the plan is working and adjust it when things change.

coverage.line: Call us and we'll walk you through coverage and how to get started.

meta.title: About Lifecare Options
meta.description: Skilled home health and Provider Attendant Services in Katy, TX since 2012. Medicare-certified, CHAP-accredited, bilingual, locally owned.

hero.headline: Caring for Katy families since 2012.
hero.intro: Lifecare Options is a locally owned home health company based in Katy, TX. Since 2012 we have brought two kinds of care into the home: Medicare-certified skilled nursing and therapy for clinical recovery, and Provider Attendant Services for everyday help with daily living.
hero.photoAlt: A nurse checking an older adult's blood pressure at home.

story.title: Locally owned, and built around the home, since 2012.
story.p1: Lifecare Options started in Katy in 2012 with a straightforward idea: people recover and live better at home, with the right kind of help behind them. For some, that means skilled nurses and therapists following them home after a hospital stay. For others, it means a trained attendant showing up for bathing, meals, and the everyday tasks that keep daily life safe and steady.
story.p2: Today our team includes registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, physical and occupational therapists, speech therapists, medical social workers, home health aides, and attendants who provide long-term, everyday support. Every skilled care plan is coordinated directly with the patient's physician; every attendant assignment is built around the person, not a checklist.
story.p3: We are not a national franchise. The people who answer your call are the same ones who come to your door, whether that is a nurse managing a recovery plan or an attendant who shows up, visit after visit, for the long run.
story.mission: To bring the right kind of care home, skilled clinical support for recovery and steady everyday help for daily living, so every person we serve can stay safe, comfortable, and as independent as possible.

band.headline: People do better at home, whether they are recovering from a hospital stay or simply need a hand with daily life. We make sure the right care follows them there.

values.title: How we show up, for every kind of care we provide.
values.card1Body: Our nurses and therapists meet Medicare and CHAP standards, and every visit is documented and shared with your physician. Quality is built into our workflow, not added on top.
values.card2Body: Care works best when the person stays in control of their routine. Our care team, clinical and attendant alike, works around your schedule and preferences, not the other way around.
values.card3Body: We communicate directly with your physician and specialist offices, and keep families in the loop on attendant care. If your care plan changes, everyone on your team knows before your next visit.
values.card4Body: Our team provides care in English and Spanish. No patient should have to navigate their health in a language that is not their own.

credentials.sinceFoundedBody: In continuous operation since 2012, serving Katy, Fort Bend, and Harris counties.

meta.title: Careers at Lifecare Options
meta.description: Join our team of nurses, therapists, and aides serving families in greater Houston. Bilingual staff welcome. Explore open positions.

hero.headline: Care for people, close to home.
hero.photoAlt: A therapist helping an older man walk with a walker at home.

why.title: A team worth joining.
why.card1Body: You will know your patients and your colleagues. There are no hand-offs to strangers. The same nurses and aides follow their patients through recovery.
why.card2Body: Home health is not floor nursing. You go to the patient, spend focused time, and make decisions. The work is clinical and direct.
why.card3Body: Clinical decisions stay with clinicians. Our nurses and therapists set the standard for care, and leadership listens when something needs to change.
why.card4Body: We work around the realities of caregiving. Schedules are built collaboratively so you can do your best work without burning out.

clinical.title: Clinical roles
clinical.intro: Skilled care, one patient at a time. We hire RNs, LVNs, and therapists for one-on-one, in-home clinical work — not floor nursing.
clinical.role1Body: Skilled nursing visits, wound care, medication management, and care planning in the patient's home.
clinical.role2Body: Help patients rebuild mobility, strength, and balance after surgery or a health setback.
clinical.role3Body: Support patients relearning the daily living skills that keep them independent at home.
clinical.role4Body: Work with patients on communication and swallowing recovery, often after a stroke.
clinical.role5Body: Connect patients and families to community resources and help them navigate what comes next.

attendant.title: Attendant roles
attendant.intro: Everyday support that keeps people home. You do not need a nursing license or prior healthcare experience to make a real difference here. We provide training, and we build schedules around real life.
attendant.role1Body: Help with bathing, dressing, grooming, and mobility — the hands-on care that makes daily life manageable.
attendant.role2Body: Meal preparation, light housekeeping, and errands that keep a household running.
attendant.role3Body: Conversation, presence, and a familiar face — for many clients, this matters as much as any task.
attendant.note: No prior healthcare experience required. Training is provided, and we work to build steady, flexible hours.

meta.title: Refer a Patient
meta.description: Physicians and discharge planners refer for skilled home health. Families, case managers, and community partners can refer directly for attendant support.

hero.headline: Refer a patient in minutes.
hero.intro: Physicians and discharge planners can send clinical orders for skilled home health. Families, case managers, and community partners can call to start a conversation about attendant support directly, no physician order needed.
hero.photoAlt: A home-health nurse arriving at a patient's home.

ways.title: Phone or fax, whichever fits your workflow.
ways.callBody: Speak directly with our intake team. We will confirm receipt, answer questions, and begin the coordination process right away.
ways.faxBody: Send orders, face sheets, or clinical notes to our secure fax line. We confirm receipt and follow up the same business day.

paths.title: Skilled care and everyday support work a little differently.
paths.clinicalBody: Skilled home health, such as nursing or therapy following a hospital stay, is typically ordered by a physician or arranged through a hospital discharge planner. We coordinate the plan of care with the treating physician.
paths.communityBody: Attendant and everyday support does not require a physician order first. Families, case managers, social workers, and community partners can call us directly to start that conversation.

next.title: What to expect after you refer.
next.step1: We reach out to the patient or family, usually within one business day of receiving the referral.
next.step2: We review coverage details and eligibility with you at no cost.
next.step3: We work with the patient's physician to build an individualized plan of care.
next.step4: A skilled clinician completes the initial home visit.
next.step5: We share progress notes with the referring provider to keep your team informed.

who.title: We work with the whole care team.
who.card1Body: Primary care physicians and specialists can initiate a referral by phone or fax. We handle prior authorization and benefit verification.
who.card2Body: Hospital discharge planners can coordinate directly with our intake team to arrange home care before the patient leaves the facility.
who.card3Body: Community and healthcare case managers can refer patients and receive regular updates on progress and plan-of-care changes.
who.card4Body: Family members and caregivers can start a referral directly, especially for attendant and everyday support, no physician order required. For skilled home health, we will coordinate with the treating physician.

meta.title: Remote Patient Monitoring
meta.description: Daily vital-sign tracking from home with nurse review. Available to eligible home health patients in our service area.

hero.headline: Daily check-ins, without leaving home.
hero.intro: Connected home devices track your vital signs every day. A nurse reviews the data and can respond quickly if something changes.
hero.photoAlt: A nurse checking an older adult's vital signs at home.

advantages.title: Why monitor from home.
advantages.card1Body: Daily readings help our nurses notice a shift in your blood pressure, oxygen level, or weight early, when it is often easier to address.
advantages.card2Body: When changes are caught early, many issues can be handled at home. That may reduce emergency visits and hospital stays.
advantages.card3Body: Ongoing clinical oversight lets you keep living independently in familiar surroundings, with a professional team keeping watch between visits.
advantages.card4Body: Readings flow directly to our nurses. If something looks off, we reach out. You are never watching alone.
advantages.card5Body: Loved ones can rest easier knowing a professional team is keeping watch between visits.
advantages.card6Body: Daily data helps your care team fine-tune your plan, which may help keep things steadier over time.

who.title: People who benefit from closer watching.
who.card1Body: Heart failure, COPD, diabetes, and high blood pressure all benefit from steady, day-to-day oversight.
who.card2Body: The weeks after a hospital discharge can be a fragile time. Monitoring helps bridge the gap between the hospital and home.
who.card3Title: Living alone or aging in place
who.card3Body: When no one is nearby to notice a change, connected monitoring becomes a constant, watchful presence.
who.card4Body: Track recovery vitals at home and flag complications early, without repeated trips back to the clinic.

coverage.title: Often covered. We find out for you.
coverage.body: Coverage varies by plan. We verify your benefits at no cost and no obligation before anything begins, so you know exactly what to expect.
coverage.note: Eligibility is determined individually. Call us and we will walk you through your options.

meta.title: Accessibility
meta.description: Lifecare Options works to make this website accessible to everyone. Contact us if you run into a barrier or need help.

hero.headline: Care that's open to everyone.
hero.intro: Every patient, family member, and referring provider should be able to use this site, whatever tools they rely on. We build with that in mind and keep improving.

commitment.title: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 AA.
commitment.body: We work to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA, the widely used standard for accessible web design and the benchmark referenced under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Conformance is an ongoing process, not a one-time certification.

done.title: Accessibility measures in this site.
done.item1: A skip-to-content link at the top of every page lets keyboard users bypass navigation.
done.item2: Semantic HTML landmarks and a clear heading structure help screen readers orient users.
done.item3: All interactive elements are keyboard operable, with a visible focus outline.
done.item4: Animations respect the system "reduce motion" preference.
done.item5: Meaningful images include descriptive text alternatives.
done.item6: Colors are chosen with readable contrast in mind.

ongoing.title: Accessibility is never finished.
ongoing.body: We continue to review and improve as we build. If any part of this site is hard to use, tell us and we will work with you to get you what you need.

contact.title: Hit a barrier? We want to help.
contact.body: Reach our team directly. Let us know the page and what got in your way, and we will respond as quickly as we can.
